cues.text: Washing dishes
Virgil van Dijk was born in 1991 in Breda, in the Netherlands.
At eight, he joined the youth academy of a club called Willem II.
As a teenager, he also had a part-time job washing dishes in a restaurant.
He worked on the days when he did not have training or a match.
Stack the plates.
Virgil worked hard at the restaurant and at training.
Doing a job well, even a small one, teaches you to keep going.
Hard work in any job teaches you something.
Too many limits?
At Willem II, Virgil was not seen as good enough.
One coach said he had too many limitations, and the club did not offer him a contract.
Being told you are not good enough is hard, especially when you are young.
Flip the sign.
But Virgil was still growing.
At seventeen, he grew about 18 centimetres, and he moved from right-back to centre-back, the position in the middle of the defence.
His new height and strength helped him win the ball in the air.
Bodies grow at different times. Don’t let one opinion stop you.
A new chance
In 2010, when he was nineteen, Virgil left Willem II and joined FC Groningen, another Dutch club.
A scout there had seen something special in him.
Moving to a new club, in a city far from home, was a fresh start.
Open the door.
On 1 May 2011, Virgil played his first professional match for Groningen.
He was finally a professional footballer.
If one door closes, look for another. Someone may see what others missed.
Very ill in hospital
Soon after his twentieth birthday, Virgil became very ill.
A problem with his appendix turned into a serious infection, and he needed an emergency operation.
He spent thirteen days in hospital and lost a lot of weight.
It was a frightening time for him and his family.
Lift the rain cloud.
Getting better took months of rest and patience.
By the summer of 2012, Virgil was back with his team.
His body had needed time, and he had given it that time.
Getting better from an illness takes time. Rest, patience and people who care help you heal.
Step by step
In 2013, Virgil joined Celtic in Scotland, where he won the league twice.
In 2015, he moved to Southampton in England.
Each move was one more step up.
Climb the steps.
In January 2018, Liverpool signed him.
At that time it was the biggest fee ever paid for a defender.
The teenager who had washed dishes was now one of the most wanted defenders in the world.
A slow climb is still a climb. Keep taking the next step.
Champion and captain
In 2019, Virgil won the Champions League with Liverpool, and he was named UEFA’s Men’s Player of the Year.
He came second for the Ballon d’Or.
In 2020, he hurt his knee badly, and he worked for months to come back.
He showed that you can come back after a big injury too.
Raise the trophy.
In 2023, Virgil became Liverpool’s captain.
The teenager who was not offered a contract had become one of the best defenders in the world.
A late start is not a slow finish. Keep growing.
